Detail:
Container 48a2201c (refiner) has been running since 22:09:47Z and emitted exactly one heartbeat at launch (state: WORKING). It has produced zero BRC proposals, zero STATUS/progress messages, and zero subsequent heartbeats in 405 seconds. The overseer_silent_agent_threshold_seconds config is 600s — the refiner will breach it in approximately 195s. Both reviewer agents (reviewer_refine, reviewer_agent_design) are healthy and polling normally. The advisor gate opened at cycle 7 (414s elapsed). No container crash detected; the container reports status=running. The stall may indicate the refiner is stuck on a long Confluence/Jira research loop, context overflow, or a silent exception that did not terminate the process.

Recommended action:
Monitor for proposal in next 2 cycles (~120s). If refiner remains silent at 600s, use egg-orch to nudge or restart the refiner container. Check refiner container logs for exceptions or infinite loops.

subject: Proposal from refiner
body: Refiner proposal v1 for issue #3023 — orchestrator-driven on-demand agent spawning. Lift the BRC event-pump loop out of agent pods into the orchestrator so a pod exists only when a role has an actionable event (next_action != "wait"). Recommends Option A: orchestrator-side per-event spawner that reuses the existing per-event primitives (`_derive_next_action` at `orchestrator/routes/consensus.py:280-406`, `compose_event_prompt` at `orchestrator/routes/event_prompt.py:337-447`, durable per-role BRC memory, `spawn_specific_roles` at `orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py:378-400`, `resolve_agent_model` from #2769) plus per-role worktree-PVC and per-role gateway-session reuse paid once per phase (not per spawn). Options B (lift only the wait) fails the primary goal; C (status quo) fails both goals; D (fresh worktree+session per event) blows the cold-start budget. Registered 6 HITL decisions covering operator-decidable scope/intent (cold-start budget, gateway-session lifecycle, idle-budget alert owner, rollout shape, consensus_wrapper.py retirement scope, overseer-agent scope) and 5 open feedback questions (resource-saving target, debug-shell affordance, in-flight PVC work in #2866 / #3017, #2958 streaming-commits adjacency, idle-budget tuning). Per the analysis.md template guidance, slice-DAG decomposition is deferred to the architect in the plan phase. Foundation is already in place from #2908 slice-3/4 (stateless per-event composer, durable memory, prefix-cache-preserving prompt shape) — this is a topology change, not an algorithm change.

payload.risk_considered: Risks considered and surfaced as HITL decisions: (1) cold-start latency per spawn — cq-1 sets operator budget; the recommended Option A explicitly pre-warms worktree PVC + gateway session to bound this. (2) Gateway session lifecycle inversion (orchestrator now owns the keep-alive that the wrapper subshell owned) — cq-2 picks the lifecycle shape; today's session_manager idle/TTL semantics are preserved. (3) Loss of the operator-visible 30-min idle-budget OVERSEER_ALERT — cq-3 picks the replacement owner (orchestrator drop-in vs. phase-level vs. drop). (4) Touches the orchestrator's hot run loop in routes/pipelines.py (mid-decomposition under #2261 slice-15) — cq-4 picks the rollout flag shape so the change can be reverted per-pipeline during burn-in. (5) Wrapper-retirement scope — cq-5 ensures the SIGTERM/cleanup contract today's wrapper provides at consensus_wrapper.py:117-124 is not silently dropped. (6) Overseer agents are on a different lifecycle today — cq-6 forces an explicit scope call rather than accidentally widening the change. (7) Cache TTL discipline noted as a constraint: consecutive events for the same role must land inside the ≥60min server-side prefix cache TTL; high-volume implement-phase NACK loops are the stress case. (8) Worktree lifecycle preservation noted as a constraint: per-role PVC reuse across spawns is non-negotiable for the cold-start budget.

subject: ACK from reviewer_agent_design for refiner
body:
ACK from agent-design lens (criteria in shared/prompts/agent-design-criteria.md). The refine analysis for #3023 (orchestrator-driven on-demand agent spawning) introduces no agent-design anti-patterns and actually improves several:

1. **Agent SDK preserved (anti-patterns #6, #7)**: The proposed pod entrypoint under Option A is `python3 -m egg_agent --model X --max-turns N` with the composed prompt on stdin — exactly the SDK entrypoint declared in `shared/egg_agent/__main__.py` (stdin path at line 47, `--model`/`--max-turns` flags at lines 35/36). No raw Anthropic SDK or HTTP calls are introduced; the change moves *toward* a cleaner Agent SDK invocation by collapsing the in-pod bash event-pump (`consensus_wrapper.py:102-715`) to a single exec.

2. **Short model aliases preserved (anti-pattern #8)**: The plan reuses the existing `resolve_agent_model(role, …).claude_code_alias` decision (`concurrent_executor.py:472-485`) per spawn — no hardcoded model IDs. `egg_agent`'s `--model` default is `opus[1m]` (alias, not full ID). EGG201 invariant intact.

3. **Pre-fetching / orienting balance (anti-pattern #1)**: `compose_event_prompt` (`event_prompt.py:337-447`) stays unchanged, including its 10 KB envelope cap, 2 KB memory cap, and tail-position memory excerpt (`event_prompt.py:28, 75, 413-436`). Bounded orientation is preserved; nothing is being bulked up. The analysis correctly identifies that the Anthropic/LiteLLM prefix cache is server-side, ≥60 min TTL, and pod-independent — so cache-hit rate is preserved across stateless pod spawns. This is good agent-mode design hygiene, not a regression.

4. **No rigid procedures / post-processing / prompt-security regressions (anti-patterns #2-#5)**: The architectural inversion is purely lifecycle (orchestrator-owned event loop vs in-pod bash loop). Agent prompt shape, MCP tool surface, sandbox model, and verdict path (`mcp__brc__*` ACK/NACK) are untouched. cq-5 explicitly contemplates deleting `consensus_wrapper.py` entirely, which would *shrink* the agent's wrapping surface to nothing.

5. **HITL scoping is appropriate**: cq-1..cq-6 (cold-start budget, gateway-session lifecycle, idle-budget owner, rollout shape, wrapper-retirement scope, overseer-scope) and feedback-1 Q1..Q5 are correctly operator-decidable. None pre-decide agent-design behavior or constrain the architect's downstream agent-prompt shape.

6. **Plan-phase scope respected**: The slice-DAG decomposition is deferred to the architect (per analysis.md template guidance and the "Complexity Assessment" section). The runtime-primitive table inventories existing surfaces without dictating new agent-side contracts.

No blockers from the agent-design lens. Files reviewed: `.egg-state/drafts/3023-analysis.md` (full, 313 lines).

subject: ACK from reviewer_refine for refiner
body:
ACK refiner v1.

The analysis is thorough, well-grounded, and surfaces a coherent recommendation (Option A: orchestrator-side per-event spawner with per-role worktree-PVC + gateway-session reuse). The four-option comparison (A/B/C/D) is meaningfully differentiated and option-elimination is justified: B fails goal 1 (idle pods remain), C fails both goals, D blows the cold-start budget. Constraints (BRC semantics preservation, cache TTL discipline, cold-start, gateway session model, worktree lifecycle, idle-budget alert path, wrapper retirement, rollout shape, file-size discipline #2261) are explicit and well-articulated.

Verified primitive references against HEAD df4c0b7f5:
- consensus_wrapper.py:102-715 event-pump template, :531-549 check_idle_budget, :59/:68 idle/HB defaults — all confirmed at the exact lines cited
- concurrent_executor.py:323 spawn_all, :378-400 spawn_specific_roles (docstring confirms "Does not touch the consensus tracker"), :445 _spawn_agent — confirmed
- routes/consensus.py:77 _VALID_ACTIONS closed set, :280 _derive_next_action — confirmed
- routes/event_prompt.py:337 compose_event_prompt — confirmed

Open-question scope audit (plan-vs-refine rubric per _get_refine_review_criteria §5):
- cq-1 (cold-start budget): operator SLO — legitimate refine HITL.
- cq-2 (gateway-session lifecycle): borderline but option (c) "breaks per-role audit and per-role model routing from #2769" is user-visible behaviour — operator should choose.
- cq-3 (idle-budget alert owner): the stuck-phase-transition anomaly tag is operator-visible signal — legitimate refine HITL.
- cq-4 (rollout shape): risk-tolerance question explicitly framed against #2908's "revert by git" precedent — external commitment / operator policy.
- cq-5 (consensus_wrapper.py retirement scope): borderline. The "delete entirely vs thin shim" axis is partly planner-decidable from SIGTERM-contract research; the "coexistence flag (EGG_ON_DEMAND=1)" axis (option 3) is genuine migration risk-tolerance. Not strong enough to NACK alone because the kubelet SIGTERM contract is user-visible operational behaviour the operator can weigh in on.
- cq-6 (overseer-agents scope): pure in/out-of-scope question — textbook refine HITL.

Feedback bundle (Q1–Q5) is appropriately open-ended and operator-decidable (resource-saving target, debug-shell affordance, in-flight #2866/#3017 PVC work, #2958 streaming-commits adjacency, idle-budget tuning).

Contract verified: all 6 decisions (cq-1..cq-6) and 1 feedback bundle (feedback-1) are registered. Recommendation, complexity assessment (high — cross-cutting), and runtime-primitive table are clear and actionable for the planner. No NACK-blocking issues.
